subject.title: fix(autoreview): allow safe Python runtime references

question: Does the new Python runtime-reference grammar remain sufficiently fail-closed for secret-bearing diffs to become an approved autoreview scanner boundary?
rationale: The patch has no demonstrated correctness defect, but deciding which parsed source forms may bypass a secret-like finding is a security-policy choice that test coverage alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve narrow grammar
options.body: Accept the AST- and token-based allow path and its hardening corpus as the supported Python reference boundary.

options.title: Require inspectable proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but request a redacted failing-before and passing-after transcript from the motivating downstream diff before approval.

options.title: Retain strict rejection
options.body: Decline the allow path and continue requiring callers to rewrite or isolate secret-looking Python assignments before autoreview.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow grammar
recommendation.body: Accept the AST- and token-based allow path and its hardening corpus as the supported Python reference boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows they introduced and repeatedly evolved the autoreview helper and its review-safety behavior.
